html:
The Roman invasion of Britain in 43 CE, ordered by the emperor Claudius, which began nearly four centuries of Roman rule over most of the island.

Since Caesar's invasions a century earlier, southern British kings had traded with Rome, and some were its allies. When one of them, Verica, was driven out and fled to Rome, Claudius, who needed a military triumph, had his excuse. Aulus Plautius crossed with four legions, one of them under the future emperor Vespasian, and won river battles on the Medway and the Thames. Claudius came himself for about sixteen days, with elephants, to enter Camulodunum, now Colchester.

The conquest took decades:

  • Caratacus fought on in Wales until he was handed over in 51 CE;
  • Boudica's revolt nearly drove the Romans out in 60 to 61 CE;
  • Agricola pushed deep into Scotland in the 80s CE.

England and Wales became the province of Britannia. Rome never held the far north, and later fixed its frontier with Hadrian's Wall. Roman rule ended around 410 (see End of Roman rule in Britain).
sum: The Roman invasion of Britain in 43 CE, ordered by the emperor Claudius, which began nearly four centuries of Roman rule over most of the island.
